title: Teriyaki Chicken Rice Bowls
seoTitle: Teriyaki Chicken Rice Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Glossy teriyaki chicken with rice and crisp vegetables
subtitle: Glossy teriyaki chicken with rice and crisp vegetables
description: Jasmine rice with homemade teriyaki chicken, broccoli, carrots, snap peas, edamame, and sesame.

steps.title: Cut and stage teriyaki ingredients
steps.instruction: Cube thighs to 1-inch pieces, cut carrots into thin matchsticks, separate broccoli florets, and trim snap peas. Whisk soy, brown sugar, ginger, garlic, cornstarch, and water in a cold bowl. Keep edamame and green onions ready beside the stove; thick carrot coins will still be raw when peas go limp.

steps.title: Steam the jasmine rice
steps.instruction: Rinse rice, bring it and measured salted water to a boil in a lidded pot, then simmer low 15 minutes. Rest it covered 10 minutes before fluffing. Do not peek while it cooks: escaping steam leaves a hard center and tempts you to add water too late.

steps.title: Prepare chicken for a hard sear
steps.instruction: Pat chicken dry and season lightly with pepper; the teriyaki supplies plenty of salt. Heat a wide skillet over medium-high until oil shimmers and set a clean hotel pan nearby. Wet chicken cools the skillet and produces pale pieces, so blot it before it touches the oil.

steps.title: Brown the teriyaki chicken
steps.instruction: Sear chicken 8–10 minutes, turning after a crust forms, until browned and 165°F in the largest piece. Move it to the hotel pan before sauce goes in. Chicken left in the skillet while the sweet glaze reduces will overcook before the sauce thickens.

steps.title: Stir-fry the vegetables
steps.instruction: Use a second wok over high heat: cook carrots 3 minutes, add broccoli and snap peas for 4 minutes, then edamame for the final minute. Toss until bright with browned edges and no puddle in the pan. Vegetables that leak water need more pan space, not more heat.

steps.title: Reduce the teriyaki glaze
steps.instruction: Pour the sauce into the emptied chicken skillet over medium heat and whisk 2–3 minutes until it coats a spoon. Return chicken and turn until glossy. Do not walk away once it bubbles; sugar moves from syrupy to burnt quickly on a hot flat-top.

steps.title: Hold the hot bowl pans
steps.instruction: Cover rice, glazed chicken, and vegetables in separate hotel pans above 140°F. Stir a spoonful of glaze through chicken before holding so the pieces do not dry at the edges. Keep sesame and onion cold and dry; steam from a hot pan makes both lose their fresh crunch. Target oven/smoker temperature: 200°F.

steps.title: Portion the rice bowls
steps.instruction: Scoop jasmine rice into each bowl, lay chicken across the center, and add vegetables alongside in distinct sections. Spoon only a little extra glaze over the chicken. Pooling sauce beneath the rice makes the bottom mushy by the time the last bowl reaches the table.

steps.title: Garnish the teriyaki bowls
steps.instruction: Sprinkle sesame seeds and green onions over the chicken, then offer chili crisp separately at the end of the line. Toasted sesame belongs on last; folding it into hot rice hides both its aroma and its crunch.

steps.title: Serve the teriyaki supper
steps.instruction: Set bowls on the pass with mandarin segments and reserve covered hot pans for late crews. Put extra glaze in a small warm pitcher, not directly over every bowl. This keeps sweetness adjustable and keeps the service table from getting sticky.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover teriyaki chicken — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool teriyaki chicken and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Cut carrots thinner than snap peas so they finish in the same pan.
Rookie tip: Keep teriyaki below a hard boil once it thickens or the sugar scorches fast.
Use thighs for the best hold quality when dinner gets delayed.
Prep tip: Toast sesame seeds in a dry pan while the rice rests.
Rookie tip: Sauce the chicken off the main sear heat so the glaze stays glossy, not burnt.
tonightSpread: Sides: Mandarin orange segments, miso soup cups
Condiments: Chili crisp, extra teriyaki, sesame seeds
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool teriyaki chicken in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Fry the rice and vegetables the next day with a scrambled egg.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It is familiar takeout comfort with controlled sweetness, a lot of vegetables, and fast bowl-line service.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: whisk teriyaki sauce and cut vegetables a day ahead. Storage: refrigerate chicken, rice, and vegetables separately for 3 days. Reheating: sprinkle rice with water, cover, and heat rice and chicken to 165°F; add sesame after reheating.
substitutions: Use brown rice instead of jasmine rice.
